question.problem:
Find $y(t)$ given that the Laplace transform of the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}(t)+y(t)=4{t}^{3}+24t,\,y(0)=0,\,{y}^{′}(0)=0
$$

is given by

$$
{s}^{2}Y(s)+Y(s)=\frac{24(1+{s}^{2})}{{s}^{4}}.
$$

The solution is $y(t)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}Y(s)+Y(s) & =\frac{24(1+{s}^{2})}{{s}^{4}} \\ ({s}^{2}+1)Y(s) & =\frac{24(1+{s}^{2})}{{s}^{4}} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{24}{{s}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

which is valid for $s>0.$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}(Y(s)) & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{24}{{s}^{4}}\} \\ y(t) & =4{L}^{-1}\{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}\} \\ y(t) & =4{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
